q1.answer: Backstage decided (ADR007) that any fetch or XMLHttpRequest in tests should be mocked with msw's express-style route handlers, as react-testing-library recommends, instead of each test mocking fetch its own way. Mocking at the network layer also exercises the real fetchApi/URL-building path; msw 2.x (http/HttpResponse) is used because msw 1.x interceptors don't capture native fetch properly (ADR014 consequences).

q2.answer: ADR014 (Proper use of HTTP fetching libraries, which supersedes ADR013's node-fetch recommendation) says frontend plugins and packages should prefer fetchApiRef; injecting the fetch implementation lets the app adorn calls with auth and other information and track metrics, rather than hard-wiring a third-party fetch library. NotificationsClient is a frontend client, so it takes the FetchApi wired from fetchApiRef in plugin.ts.

q3.answer: ADR010 makes Luxon the standard date library for core packages and plugins for formatting the native Date can't easily do (like the relative 'a day ago' text from toRelative()). Moment.js was rejected for its large bundle size, mutable state and being sunset; Luxon is immutable, uses modern Intl APIs and keeps one library/smaller bundles.

q4.answer: ADR006 says to avoid React.FC/React.SFC in new code because they implicitly add a children prop and don't support generic types on children (the reason create-react-app dropped React.FC from its template). Components instead type their props parameter directly, adding children explicitly when needed.

q5.answer: ADR004 requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files down to src/index.ts, with each index re-exporting only its immediate children (wildcard for index-to-index, enumerated names for non-index files). This makes the package's public boundary predictable: you can tell whether a symbol is public by walking index files toward the root, which deep re-exports from src/index.ts would break.
